newsitem.title: USA: ABC/Money consumer comfort index steady at -11.
newsitem.headline: ABC/Money consumer comfort index steady at -11.

text.p: The Money Magazine/ABC News consumer comfort index held steady at -11 in the week ended August 25.

"Americans have remained relatively cheery about the current shape of the economy and their own finances, but their views of today's buying climate have begun to dim," said a report released with the index.

The survey, this time with 1,046 respondents, polls consumers nationwide about the national economy, their own finances and their willingness to spend money. The poll has a margin of error of plus/minus 3.5 percent.
Forty percent of consumers polled rated the economy positively, pulling the survey's economic index up two points to -20.
Fifty-eight percent rated their own finances positively, and 35 percent said now is a good time to spend.

"Regionally, northeasterners' rising faith in their finances, as well as in the economy and spending, helped confidence rebound in that area," the survey said. "By contrast, attitudes slipped to a six-week low in the Midwest."
